chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Abī ʿUbaydah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who had a wife in al-Baṣrah, then committed illicit intercourse in al-Kūfah, that stoning is to be averted from him and he is to be given the hadd punishment of the fornicator.” And he said: “He ruled regarding an imprisoned man in the prison who had a wife in his house in the town, while he could not reach her, and he committed zina while in prison.” He said: “He is to be flogged with the flogging, and stoning is to be averted from him.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, whose judicial ruling is being cited
key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as the hadd punishment in certain cases of zina
key_terms.السِّجْنِ: prison, the state preventing access to one's spouse
key_terms.حَدَّ الزَّانِي: the prescribed legal punishment of the fornicator
key_terms.يُدْرَأُ: it is to be averted or warded off

ai.seo_question: When is rajm averted from a married man who commits zina according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning zina in cases where a man has a wife but is effectively unable to access her due to distance or imprisonment. In such cases, the punishment of rajm is averted, and the hadd of flogging is applied instead, indicating a distinction in legal status based on practical access to one's spouse.
